name: Hurricane Katrina
kicker: 2005 storm that flooded New Orleans · One of the costliest U.S. disasters
briefing: In late August 2005, Hurricane Katrina swept across the Gulf and slammed into Louisiana and Mississippi. In New Orleans, a city that lies mostly below sea level, levees and floodwalls failed, and water covered about 80 percent of the city. More than 1,800 people died, tens of thousands waited for help at the Superdome and the city’s convention center, and the government’s response was widely criticized.
answerHtml: Hurricane Katrina (prompt on hurricane; do not accept “Hurricane Rita”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Four days before its most famous landfall, this storm crossed southern Florida as a Category 1 hurricane, coming ashore between Hallandale Beach and Aventura. It then strengthened over warm Gulf waters into a Category 5 storm with winds of about 175 miles per hour.
tossups.r: Levee failures during this storm flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans. For 10 points, name this August 2005 hurricane.

tossups.p: On the morning of August 29, 2005, this storm made landfall near Buras, Louisiana, as a Category 3 hurricane, then struck again near the mouth of the Pearl River on the Louisiana–Mississippi border. It had formed near the Bahamas six days earlier.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this hurricane that flooded New Orleans after its levees failed.

tossups.p: This storm pushed a wall of seawater about 28 feet high into Pass Christian, Mississippi, the highest storm surge ever measured in the United States. It also badly damaged Beauvoir [“BOH-vwahr”], Jefferson Davis’s last home, in Biloxi [“buh-LUK-see”].
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane that devastated the Gulf Coast of Mississippi and flooded New Orleans.

tossups.p: During this disaster, floodwalls along the 17th Street and London Avenue Canals gave way, letting Lake Pontchartrain [“PONCH-er-train”] pour into the city, and a breach in the Industrial Canal flooded the Lower Ninth Ward. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers had built those floodwalls.
tossups.r: About 80 percent of New Orleans ended up underwater. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane.

tossups.p: On August 28, 2005, Mayor Ray Nagin [“NAY-gin”] ordered the first mandatory evacuation in his city’s history as this storm approached. Many residents without cars could not leave, and the city opened a “refuge of last resort” for them.
tossups.r: Tens of thousands of people took shelter in the Louisiana Superdome during this storm. For 10 points, name this hurricane.

tossups.p: Thousands of people stranded by this disaster were taken by bus to the Astrodome in Houston, Texas, a city that took in more than 100,000 evacuees in all. Many of those buses left from a downtown stadium where people had sheltered for days.
tossups.r: That stadium was the Louisiana Superdome. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane that flooded New Orleans.

tossups.p: Coast Guard admiral Thad Allen took charge of federal relief efforts in September 2005 after FEMA director Michael Brown was sent back to Washington, and Brown resigned days later amid widespread criticism of the federal response to this disaster.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane during which levee failures flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans.

tossups.p: The U.S. Coast Guard rescued more than 33,000 people during this disaster, many of them lifted by helicopter from the roofs of flooded houses. Army general Russel Honoré led the military task force sent to help.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this August 2005 hurricane that left about 80 percent of New Orleans underwater.

tossups.p: A special House committee’s 2006 report on the response to this disaster was titled _A Failure of Initiative_. The committee examined problems at every level of government, from the city to the state to FEMA.
tossups.r: That disaster killed more than 1,800 people. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane that flooded New Orleans.

tossups.p: After the 2005 season, the World Meteorological Organization retired this storm’s name and replaced it with Katia. That record-breaking season was the first in which forecasters ran out of names and used letters of the Greek alphabet.
tossups.r: Less than a month after this storm, Hurricane Rita struck the Gulf Coast. For 10 points, name this hurricane that flooded New Orleans in August 2005.

tossups.p: Spike Lee’s four-part 2006 documentary _When the Levees Broke: A Requiem in Four Acts_ examines this disaster and its aftermath. The HBO drama _Treme_ [“truh-MAY”], named for a historic neighborhood, follows people rebuilding their lives three months after it.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane that flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans.

tossups.p: An NFL team played its 2005 home games in San Antonio, Baton Rouge, and New Jersey after this disaster damaged its stadium. That team’s return home in September 2006 was a nationally televised Monday night game against the Atlanta Falcons.
tossups.r: That team, the Saints, plays in New Orleans. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane.

tossups.p: The rock-and-roll pioneer Fats Domino, who had stayed in his home in the Lower Ninth Ward, was rescued from the floodwaters during this disaster. Water had poured into that neighborhood when the wall of a nearby canal broke.
tossups.r: Levee and floodwall failures during this storm left about 80 percent of New Orleans underwater. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane.

tossups.p: A shipping channel called the Mississippi River–Gulf Outlet, nicknamed “Mister Go,” was blamed for funneling this storm’s surge toward the city’s eastern neighborhoods, and Congress later had it closed. Less than a month after this storm, Hurricane Rita flooded some of those areas again.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this August 2005 hurricane during which about 80 percent of New Orleans flooded.

tossups.p: Louisiana governor Kathleen Blanco and Mississippi governor Haley Barbour led their states through this disaster, which destroyed whole neighborhoods in Biloxi and Gulfport. It became one of the costliest natural disasters in American history.
tossups.r: More than 1,800 people died. For 10 points, name this 2005 hurricane that flooded New Orleans.

clues.t: Levee and floodwall failures flooded about 80 percent of New Orleans
Made landfall on August 29, 2005, in Louisiana, then struck Mississippi
More than 1,800 people died; one of the deadliest and costliest U.S. hurricanes
Tens of thousands of people sheltered in the Louisiana Superdome
The government response was widely criticized; FEMA director Michael Brown resigned in September 2005
George W. Bush was president; Kathleen Blanco was governor of Louisiana and Haley Barbour governor of Mississippi
A breach in the Industrial Canal flooded the Lower Ninth Ward
Floodwalls on the 17th Street and London Avenue Canals failed, letting Lake Pontchartrain pour in
Mayor Ray Nagin ordered the first mandatory evacuation in New Orleans history (August 28, 2005)
Many evacuees were bused to the Astrodome in Houston, which took in more than 100,000 people
Hurricane Rita struck less than a month later (September 24, 2005) and re-flooded parts of New Orleans
Wrecked the Mississippi coast, including Biloxi and Gulfport
First crossed southern Florida as a Category 1 hurricane (August 25, 2005); had formed near the Bahamas
Peaked as a Category 5 storm over the Gulf, then made landfall near Buras, Louisiana, as a Category 3
Storm surge of about 28 feet at Pass Christian, Mississippi, the highest ever measured in the U.S.
Badly damaged Beauvoir, Jefferson Davis’s last home, in Biloxi
Coast Guard admiral Thad Allen took over federal relief; the Coast Guard rescued more than 33,000 people
Army general Russel Honoré led the military relief task force
A special House committee’s 2006 report on the response was titled _A Failure of Initiative_
Its name was retired and replaced by Katia; 2005 was the first season to use Greek-letter storm names
Spike Lee’s documentary _When the Levees Broke_ (2006); the HBO drama _Treme_ is set three months after it
The Saints played their 2005 home games elsewhere and returned to the Superdome in September 2006
Fats Domino was rescued from his flooded home in the Lower Ninth Ward
The Mississippi River–Gulf Outlet (“Mister Go”) was blamed for funneling the surge; Congress had it closed

trap.title: Katrina, not Rita
trap.body: Hurricane Katrina hit in late August 2005, and Hurricane Rita struck near the Texas–Louisiana border less than a month later, flooding parts of New Orleans again, so fall 2005 clues can point to either storm. Hurricane Harvey (2017) flooded Houston, and Hurricane Sandy (2012) battered New York and New Jersey. A tossup that asks for “this city” or “this state” wants New Orleans or Louisiana instead, and the general weather topic “Hurricanes” is a separate answer line.
trap.fix: August 29, 2005, the Superdome, the Lower Ninth Ward, the levee failures, FEMA’s Michael Brown, and the Astrodome evacuees mean Katrina. Rita means September 24, 2005, and southwest Louisiana. If the question says “this storm” or “this hurricane,” answer “Hurricane Katrina.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Hurricane Katrina (prompt on hurricane; do not accept “Hurricane Rita”)
